templates.one_way:
NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

This Non-Disclosure Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}} between:

{{PARTY_A_NAME}} ("Disclosing Party")
and
{{PARTY_B_NAME}} ("Receiving Party")

## 1. Purpose

The Receiving Party agrees to receive certain confidential and proprietary information from the Disclosing Party for the following purpose: {{PURPOSE}}.

## 2. Definition of Confidential Information

"Confidential Information" means any non-public information the Disclosing Party designates as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. This includes, but is not limited to: business plans, financial information, technical data, trade secrets, know-how, research, product plans, software, inventions, processes, formulas, technology, designs, engineering, marketing information, customer lists, and pricing.

## 3. Obligations of the Receiving Party

The Receiving Party agrees to:

a) Hold all Confidential Information in strict confidence;
b) Not disclose any Confidential Information to any third party without the Disclosing Party's prior written consent;
c) Use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose stated herein;
d) Protect the Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information, but no less than reasonable care;
e) Limit access to Confidential Information to personnel who have a strict need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set out herein;
f) Not reverse engineer, disassemble, or decompile any prototypes, software, or other tangible objects that embody the Confidential Information.

## 4. Exceptions

The Receiving Party's obligations do not apply to information that:

a) Is or becomes publicly known through no breach of this Agreement;
b) Was rightfully known to the Receiving Party before disclosure, as evidenced by written records predating this Agreement;
c) Is received from a third party without restriction and without breach of any agreement with the Disclosing Party;
d) Is independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to the Confidential Information;
e) Is required to be disclosed by applicable law, regulation, or court order — provided the Receiving Party gives the Disclosing Party prompt written notice and reasonable cooperation in seeking a protective order.

## 5. Duration

This Agreement commences on {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}} and continues for {{DURATION}} from the date of last disclosure of Confidential Information, unless earlier terminated by mutual written agreement. Confidentiality obligations survive termination for {{DURATION}}.

## 6. Return or Destruction of Materials

Upon the Disclosing Party's written request, or upon termination of this Agreement, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information — including all copies, extracts, and summaries — and shall certify such return or destruction in writing upon request.

## 7. No License

Nothing in this Agreement grants the Receiving Party any rights or licences in or to the Confidential Information, except as explicitly stated herein. No intellectual property rights are transferred or licensed by this Agreement.

## 8. No Employment or Agency Relationship

This Agreement does not create any employment, agency, joint venture, or partnership relationship between the Parties.

## 9. Remedies

The Receiving Party acknowledges that any breach of this Agreement may cause irreparable harm to the Disclosing Party for which monetary damages would be inadequate. The Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek equitable relief, including injunction and specific performance, without the requirement to post a bond, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity.

## 10. Governing Law

This Agreement is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of {{GOVERNING_LAW}}, without regard to its conflict of law provisions. The Parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of {{GOVERNING_LAW}}.

## 11. Entire Agreement

This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the disclosure of Confidential Information and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements relating thereto. Amendments must be in writing and signed by both Parties.

---

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Non-Disclosure Agreement as of {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}}.

{{PARTY_A_NAME}} (Disclosing Party)

Title: _________________________________
Date: _________________________________


{{PARTY_B_NAME}} (Receiving Party)

templates.mutual:
MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}} between:

{{PARTY_A_NAME}} ("Party A")
and
{{PARTY_B_NAME}} ("Party B")

(each a "Party" and collectively, the "Parties")

## 1. Purpose

The Parties wish to explore a potential business relationship and may disclose to each other certain confidential and proprietary information for the following purpose: {{PURPOSE}}.

## 2. Definition of Confidential Information

"Confidential Information" means any non-public information that a Party ("Disclosing Party") designates as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. This includes, but is not limited to: business plans, financial information, technical data, trade secrets, know-how, research, product plans, software, inventions, processes, formulas, technology, designs, engineering, marketing information, customer lists, and pricing.

## 3. Mutual Obligations

Each Party, when acting as the Receiving Party, agrees to:

a) Hold the other Party's Confidential Information in strict confidence;
b) Not disclose Confidential Information to any third party without the Disclosing Party's prior written consent;
c) Use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose stated herein;
d) Protect Confidential Information with the same degree of care used to protect its own confidential information, but no less than reasonable care;
e) Limit access to Confidential Information to personnel with a strict need to know who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those herein;
f) Not reverse engineer, disassemble, or decompile any tangible objects that embody the other Party's Confidential Information.

## 4. Exceptions

Obligations under this Agreement do not apply to information that:

a) Is or becomes publicly known through no breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party;
b) Was rightfully known to the Receiving Party before disclosure, as evidenced by written records predating this Agreement;
c) Is received from a third party without restriction and without breach of any obligation owed to the Disclosing Party;
d) Is independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to the Confidential Information;
e) Is required to be disclosed by law, regulation, or court order — provided the Receiving Party gives prompt written notice and reasonable cooperation in seeking a protective order.

## 5. Duration

This Agreement commences on {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}} and continues for {{DURATION}} from the date of last disclosure, unless earlier terminated by mutual written agreement. Confidentiality obligations survive termination for {{DURATION}}.

## 6. Return or Destruction of Materials

Upon request or upon termination, each Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party — including all copies, extracts, and summaries — and certify such return or destruction in writing upon request.

## 7. No License

Nothing in this Agreement grants either Party any rights or licences in or to the other Party's Confidential Information, except as explicitly stated herein. No intellectual property rights are transferred or licensed by this Agreement.

## 8. No Employment or Agency Relationship

This Agreement does not create any employment, agency, joint venture, or partnership relationship between the Parties.

## 9. Remedies

Each Party acknowledges that breach of this Agreement may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be inadequate. Each Party shall be entitled to seek equitable relief, including injunction and specific performance, without the requirement to post a bond, in addition to all other available remedies.

## 10. Governing Law

This Agreement is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of {{GOVERNING_LAW}}, without regard to its conflict of law provisions. The Parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of {{GOVERNING_LAW}}.

## 11. Entire Agreement

This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to mutual non-disclosure and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements. Amendments must be in writing and signed by both Parties.

---

freelance.template:
FREELANCE SERVICE AGREEMENT

This Freelance Service Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}} between:

{{CLIENT_NAME}} ("Client")
and
{{FREELANCER_NAME}} ("Contractor")

## 1. Services

The Contractor agrees to perform the following services for the Client:

Project: {{PROJECT_TITLE}}

Scope of Work:
{{SCOPE_OF_WORK}}

## 2. Timeline and Deadline

The Contractor agrees to complete and deliver the project by {{PROJECT_DEADLINE}}. Extensions to this deadline require mutual written agreement. The Contractor will provide reasonable progress updates upon the Client's request.

## 3. Compensation

Total Project Fee: {{TOTAL_FEE}}

Payment Schedule: {{PAYMENT_SCHEDULE}}.

Invoices are due within 14 days of receipt. Late payments are subject to a late fee of 1.5% per month on the outstanding balance. The Client agrees that work will not commence or continue until the agreed deposit has been received.

## 4. Expenses

The Client shall reimburse the Contractor for all pre-approved, reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred in the performance of the Services. Expenses must be submitted with supporting documentation within 30 days of being incurred.

## 5. Independent Contractor Status

The Contractor is an independent contractor and not an employee, partner, or agent of the Client. The Contractor is solely responsible for all taxes, insurance, superannuation, and other statutory obligations relating to the Contractor's status. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to create an employment relationship.

{{IP_OWNERSHIP_CLAUSE}}

## 7. Confidentiality

The Contractor agrees to keep confidential all non-public information, trade secrets, and proprietary data of the Client obtained in connection with the Services. The Contractor shall not disclose such information to any third party without the Client's prior written consent. This obligation survives termination of this Agreement for two (2) years.

## 8. Revisions

The scope of work includes {{REVISION_ROUNDS}} round(s) of revisions. Additional revisions beyond this scope will be billed at the Contractor's standard hourly rate, to be agreed in writing before commencing additional work.

## 9. Warranties

The Contractor warrants that:
a) The Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards;
b) To the best of the Contractor's knowledge, the deliverables will not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights;
c) The Contractor has the full right and authority to enter into this Agreement and is not bound by any conflicting obligations.

## 10. Termination

Either Party may terminate this Agreement with {{NOTICE_PERIOD}} days written notice. In the event of termination, the Client shall pay the Contractor for all Services performed and expenses incurred up to the termination date. If the Client terminates after work has commenced without cause, any deposit paid is non-refundable.

## 11. Limitation of Liability

The Contractor's total liability for any claim arising from this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid by the Client under this Agreement in the three (3) months preceding the claim. Neither Party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages.

## 12. Governing Law

This Agreement is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of {{GOVERNING_LAW}}. Any disputes shall be resolved through good-faith negotiation. Unresolved disputes shall be subject to binding arbitration or the courts of {{GOVERNING_LAW}}, as agreed by the Parties.

## 13. Entire Agreement

This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties regarding the Services and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, or agreements. Amendments must be in writing and signed by both Parties.

---

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Freelance Service Agreement as of {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}}.

{{CLIENT_NAME}} (Client)

EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

This Employment Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of {{START_DATE}} between:

{{EMPLOYER_NAME}} ("Employer")
and
{{EMPLOYEE_NAME}} ("Employee")

## 1. Position and Duties

The Employee is hired for the position of {{JOB_TITLE}} and shall perform all duties and responsibilities customarily associated with this role, as well as such additional duties as may reasonably be assigned by the Employer from time to time.

Primary Work Location: {{WORK_LOCATION}}

## 2. Employment Type and Commencement

Employment Type: {{EMPLOYMENT_TYPE}}

Start Date: {{START_DATE}}

{{PROBATION_CLAUSE}}

## 3. Compensation

Base Salary / Wage: {{COMPENSATION}}

The Employee will be paid {{PAY_FREQUENCY}}. The Employer will deduct all applicable income taxes, national insurance / social security contributions, and any other statutory deductions required by law.

## 4. Working Hours

The Employee's standard working hours are {{WORKING_HOURS}} hours per week. The Employer may require the Employee to work additional hours as reasonably necessary for the effective performance of their duties, to be compensated in accordance with applicable law and company policy.

## 5. Leave and Benefits

a) Annual Leave: {{ANNUAL_LEAVE}} days per year (in addition to statutory public holidays), accruing at a pro-rata rate.
b) Sick Leave: In accordance with applicable law and the Employer's current sick leave policy.
c) Parental Leave: In accordance with applicable law.
d) Additional benefits, if any, are set out in the Employee Handbook or as otherwise agreed in writing.

## 6. Confidentiality

The Employee agrees to maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all proprietary information, trade secrets, business strategies, client and customer lists, financial data, and other confidential information of the Employer, both during and after employment. This obligation survives termination of this Agreement indefinitely.

## 7. Intellectual Property

All work product, inventions, improvements, designs, software, code, content, and other intellectual property created by the Employee in the course of their employment — whether or not on Employer's premises or using Employer's equipment — shall be the sole and exclusive property of the Employer. The Employee hereby irrevocably assigns all such rights to the Employer and agrees to execute any documents necessary to perfect such assignment.

## 8. Non-Competition and Non-Solicitation

{{NON_COMPETE_CLAUSE}}

During employment and for {{NON_COMPETE_PERIOD}} following termination (for any reason), the Employee agrees not to:
a) Solicit or attempt to hire any employee of the Employer;
b) Solicit, divert, or attempt to take away any clients, customers, or business contacts of the Employer.

## 9. Code of Conduct

The Employee agrees to comply with all lawful Employer policies, procedures, and codes of conduct as communicated from time to time, including but not limited to the Employee Handbook, IT and data security policies, and workplace health and safety requirements.

## 10. Termination

By the Employer: The Employer may terminate this Agreement with {{NOTICE_PERIOD}} written notice, or payment in lieu of notice. The Employer may terminate the Agreement immediately and without notice for cause (including, without limitation, gross misconduct, theft, dishonesty, or material breach of this Agreement).

By the Employee: The Employee may terminate this Agreement with {{NOTICE_PERIOD}} written notice.

Upon Termination: The Employee shall promptly return all Employer property, equipment, documents, and data. The Employee's confidentiality and intellectual property obligations continue after termination.

## 11. Governing Law

This Agreement is governed by and construed in accordance with the employment laws of {{GOVERNING_LAW}}. Both Parties submit to the jurisdiction of the relevant courts of {{GOVERNING_LAW}}.

## 12. Entire Agreement

This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties regarding the Employee's employment and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, or agreements. Amendments must be in writing and signed by both Parties.

---

sla.template:
SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT

This Service Level Agreement ("SLA" or "Agreement") is entered into as of {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}} between:

{{PROVIDER_NAME}} ("Service Provider")
and
{{CLIENT_NAME}} ("Client")

## 1. Definitions

"Downtime" means any period during which the Service is unavailable or materially degraded, excluding Scheduled Maintenance and the exclusions listed in Section 8.

"Uptime" means the percentage of time in a given calendar month during which the Service is available and performing within acceptable parameters, calculated as: ((Total minutes in month − Downtime minutes) / Total minutes in month) × 100.

"Service Credits" means a reduction applied to future invoices as compensation for failure to meet the Uptime Commitment.

"Incident" means any unplanned interruption to, or reduction in the quality of, the Service.

"Response Time" means the time between initial notification of an Incident and acknowledgment by the Service Provider's support team.

## 2. Services Covered

This SLA applies to the following services (the "Service"):

{{SERVICE_DESCRIPTION}}

## 3. Uptime Guarantee

The Service Provider commits to a monthly Uptime of {{UPTIME_GUARANTEE}} (the "Uptime Commitment"). Uptime is measured on a calendar month basis. The Service Provider will maintain a public status page or provide equivalent monitoring data upon request.

## 4. Scheduled Maintenance

The Service Provider may take the Service offline for scheduled maintenance during the following window: {{MAINTENANCE_WINDOW}}. At least 48 hours' advance notice will be provided via email or status page notification. Scheduled Maintenance does not count toward Downtime calculations.

## 5. Support and Response Times

Support is available: {{SUPPORT_HOURS}}.

Incidents are classified and responded to as follows:

Critical — Complete service outage or risk of data loss: Response within {{CRITICAL_RESPONSE_TIME}}
High — Major feature unavailable or severe performance degradation: Response within {{HIGH_RESPONSE_TIME}}
Medium — Minor feature impaired, moderate impact on operations: Response within {{MEDIUM_RESPONSE_TIME}}
Low — Cosmetic issue, general enquiry, or minor inconvenience: Response within {{LOW_RESPONSE_TIME}}

Response times begin from the moment of Incident notification via the designated support channel. Out-of-hours support may have extended response times for non-Critical incidents.

## 6. Incident Reporting and Communication

The Client must report Incidents via the Service Provider's designated support channel. Incidents reported outside the designated channel may not qualify for SLA credit.

The Service Provider will:
a) Acknowledge the Incident within the applicable Response Time;
b) Provide status updates at reasonable intervals until resolution;
c) Deliver a root cause analysis for Critical Incidents within 5 business days of resolution;
d) Implement reasonable measures to prevent recurrence of the same Incident.

## 7. Service Credits

If the Service Provider fails to meet the Uptime Commitment in a given calendar month, the Client is entitled to Service Credits as follows:

Uptime 99.0% to below {{UPTIME_GUARANTEE}}: 5% of that month's fee
Uptime 95.0% to 98.99%: 10% of that month's fee
Uptime 90.0% to 94.99%: 20% of that month's fee
Uptime below 90.0%: {{SERVICE_CREDIT_CAP}} of that month's fee (maximum)

Service Credits are the Client's sole and exclusive remedy for Downtime and SLA breaches. Total credits in any calendar month shall not exceed {{SERVICE_CREDIT_CAP}} of that month's fee. To claim credits, the Client must submit a written request within 30 days of the relevant month. Credits are applied to future invoices and are not redeemable for cash.

## 8. Exclusions

The Uptime Commitment does not apply to unavailability caused by:

a) Scheduled Maintenance as defined in Section 4;
b) Acts or omissions of the Client or third parties acting on the Client's behalf;
c) The Client's own hardware, software, network, or internet connectivity failures;
d) Force majeure events including natural disasters, war, government actions, or internet infrastructure failures outside the Service Provider's control;
e) The Client's failure to meet published minimum system or browser requirements;
f) Features explicitly designated as beta or as outside the scope of this SLA;
g) DDoS attacks, security breaches, or other malicious third-party activity directed at the Service.

## 9. Measurement and Reporting

The Service Provider will maintain records of all Incidents and Uptime measurements. Monthly Uptime reports are available upon reasonable written request. The Service Provider's own monitoring systems shall be the authoritative source for Uptime calculations in the absence of a separate agreed third-party monitoring arrangement.

## 10. Escalation Procedure

If the Client is unsatisfied with the response or resolution of an Incident, the Client may escalate the matter in writing to the Service Provider's management team. The Service Provider will ensure that senior technical staff review all escalated Incidents within one business day of escalation.

## 11. Term and Review

BUSINESS PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT

This Partnership Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}} between:

{{PARTNER_A_NAME}} ("Partner A")
{{PARTNER_B_NAME}} ("Partner B"){{PARTNER_C_BLOCK}}

(each a "Partner" and collectively, the "Partners")

## 1. Formation

The Partners hereby agree to form a general partnership (the "Partnership") under the laws of {{GOVERNING_LAW}}.

## 2. Business Name and Purpose

Business Name: {{BUSINESS_NAME}}

Business Purpose: {{BUSINESS_PURPOSE}}

## 3. Term

The Partnership commences on {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}} and continues until dissolved in accordance with this Agreement.

## 4. Capital Contributions

The initial capital contributions of each Partner are:

Partner A — {{PARTNER_A_NAME}}: {{PARTNER_A_CONTRIBUTION}}
Partner B — {{PARTNER_B_NAME}}: {{PARTNER_B_CONTRIBUTION}}{{PARTNER_C_CONTRIBUTION_BLOCK}}

Additional capital contributions may only be made by unanimous written agreement. No Partner may withdraw any portion of their capital contribution without unanimous written consent, except upon dissolution.

## 5. Profit and Loss Sharing

Profits and losses shall be allocated as follows:

{{PARTNER_A_NAME}}: {{PARTNER_A_SHARE}}
{{PARTNER_B_NAME}}: {{PARTNER_B_SHARE}}{{PARTNER_C_SHARE_BLOCK}}

Distributions shall be made {{PROFIT_DISTRIBUTION}}, subject to the Partnership maintaining sufficient working capital reserves as the Partners determine.

## 6. Management and Decision-Making

{{DECISION_MAKING_CLAUSE}}

Each Partner shall devote reasonable time and effort to the Partnership and act in good faith and in the Partnership's best interests at all times.

No Partner may, without the prior written consent of all other Partners: enter into contracts exceeding [AUTHORITY_LIMIT] on behalf of the Partnership; borrow money or incur debt on behalf of the Partnership; sell or encumber any material Partnership asset; initiate or settle any litigation on behalf of the Partnership; or hire or dismiss any employee earning more than [SALARY_LIMIT] per annum.

## 7. Banking and Accounts

The Partnership shall maintain a dedicated bank account. All Partnership funds shall be deposited in this account. Withdrawals require the signature of at least two Partners (or the Managing Partner where applicable).

## 8. Intellectual Property

All intellectual property created by any Partner in the course of Partnership business — including inventions, designs, software, brand assets, and content — shall be the sole property of the Partnership. Each Partner irrevocably assigns all such rights to the Partnership. Pre-existing IP contributed at formation remains the contributing Partner's property unless documented otherwise in a written Schedule to this Agreement.

## 9. Confidentiality

Each Partner agrees to keep confidential all non-public information relating to the Partnership's business, clients, finances, and operations, both during and after their participation. This obligation survives termination for three (3) years.

## 10. Non-Competition

{{NON_COMPETE_CLAUSE}}

## 11. Admission of New Partners

New Partners may only be admitted by unanimous written consent of all existing Partners. Terms of admission must be documented in a written amendment to this Agreement.

## 12. Transfer of Partnership Interest

No Partner may sell, assign, or transfer their Partnership interest without the prior written consent of all other Partners. The remaining Partners hold a right of first refusal on any proposed transfer at fair market value.

## 13. Death, Incapacity, or Withdrawal

Upon the death, permanent incapacity, or voluntary withdrawal of a Partner, the remaining Partners may elect to: (a) continue the Partnership and purchase the departing Partner's interest at fair market value (determined by independent valuation within 60 days); or (b) dissolve the Partnership. The estate of a deceased or incapacitated Partner has no right to become a Partner without unanimous consent of remaining Partners but is entitled to receive the value of the departing Partner's interest.

## 14. Dissolution

The Partnership shall be dissolved upon: unanimous written agreement; death or incapacity where remaining Partners elect not to continue; entry of a judicial dissolution order; or illegality of the Partnership's business. Upon dissolution, assets shall be applied first to discharge liabilities, then to return capital contributions, then distributed pro-rata to Partners per their profit share.

## 15. Dispute Resolution

The Partners agree to attempt resolution of any dispute through good-faith negotiation, then mediation, before commencing legal proceedings.

## 16. Governing Law

This Agreement is governed by the laws of {{GOVERNING_LAW}}.

## 17. Entire Agreement

This Agreement supersedes all prior negotiations and agreements between the Partners regarding the Partnership. Amendments require unanimous written consent.

---

The Merchant will provide the Affiliate with a unique affiliate link, tracking code, or promotional code ("Affiliate Link"). A qualifying referral is any new customer who completes a qualifying transaction within {{COOKIE_WINDOW}} of clicking the Affiliate Link (the "Attribution Window"). The Merchant uses last-click attribution. If a customer uses multiple affiliate links, commissions will be attributed per the Merchant's standard attribution policy.
